# Give the grid a physical meaning

[Sixteen samples do not define a physical length until we say where they are.]{.lesson-deck}

[First six experiments · 1 of 6](../../start/index.qmd){.lesson-route-label}
:::

A `Domain` describes the global grid. Its dimensions count samples;
its origin and spacing assign those samples physical coordinates.
It does not allocate a solution field or choose a differential operator.

## State the geometry in one expression

```{.cpp include="model.cpp" snippet="domain" dedent=4}
```

The named argument types help the compiler distinguish sample counts,
origin and spacing. The first coordinate follows

$$
\begin{gathered}
x_i=-1+.125i, \\
i=0,\ldots,15.
\end{gathered}
$$ {#eq-coordinate}

Thus $i=3$ means $x=-.625$. Likewise, $j=5$ means $y=.5$.
`to_indices` maps that sample's coordinate back to its original index.
This exact round trip concerns grid samples; arbitrary points require
attention to the API's rounding and bounds conventions.

## Count a periodic endpoint once

The last x sample is .875, while the periodic box's upper boundary is 1.
The point at 1 is identified with the point at -1, so storing both would
duplicate a sample. A nonperiodic axis instead spans its first and last
samples. Here the nonperiodic z axis has one sample, representing a plane.

The program writes all three axes to `results/domain.csv`, including
their last sample and upper boundary. Compare those columns before
moving on to [endpoint conventions](../grid-spacing/index.qmd).

## Run your first experiment

```sh
openpfc run model.cpp input.json --launcher=none
```

The geometry is deliberately visible in `model.cpp`; this lesson's input
is empty. Change the origin or spacing, then predict the printed coordinate
before running again. Try changing the periodicity of x and compare its
reported upper boundary. This program does not initialize MPI.

The complete [source](model.cpp) and [input](input.json) are available.
Continue with [distributed ownership](../decomposition/index.qmd) or
[a first derivative](../../differentiation/periodic/index.qmd).
